subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default proactive retention policy for stale session archive artifacts beyond the existing deleted/reset, stale temp, unreferenced-artifact, and disk-budget paths?
rationale: Current source shows real partial cleanup, but broad automatic deletion affects session recovery, diagnostics, and retained history semantics that automation should not choose for maintainers.

options.title: Scope broad cleanup policy
options.body: Keep this issue open as the parent and define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts are removed under which retention rules.

options.title: Land the narrow reporting fix first
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97103 for the deleted/reset visibility subset and defer the broader proactive cleanup policy.

options.title: Split by artifact class
options.body: Close or narrow this parent only after each remaining suffix or sidecar class has a canonical issue with its safety proof preserved.

recommendation.title: Scope broad cleanup policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the parent and define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts are removed under which retention rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that the broad cleanup policy would extend at the command/operator boundary.
